mainTopic: Respect for the בית הכנסת and תפילה, the 'אגרא' sayings on where each מצוה's main reward lies, and רב הונא's teachings on מנחה, gladdening a חתן, יראת שמים, and greeting others.
overview: This amud opens by finishing the earlier discussion of הקדוש ברוך הוא's תפילין: in the arm-תפילין, all the verses are written together. It then turns to the בית הכנסת. If a regular misses a day, הקדוש ברוך הוא asks about him, and He is angry when He finds no מנין. A person who keeps a fixed place for תפילה follows אברהם אבינו. One should walk out of the בית הכנסת slowly but run in, and running to learn תורה is praised even on שבת. A list of seven 'אגרא' sayings teaches where the main reward of each מצוה lies, from running to a שיעור to the words of joy at a wedding. רב הונא calls one who prays behind the בית הכנסת facing away a רשע, and the גמרא explains the rest of his פסוק, including the shame of depending on others. The amud ends with more teachings of רבי חלבו in the name of רב הונא: be careful with מנחה (רבי יוחנן and רב נחמן בר יצחק add ערבית and שחרית), gladden a חתן at his meal, the words of one with יראת שמים are heard, and greet others first and always answer a greeting.

steps.title: All the verses are written together in the arm-תפילין
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the earlier discussion of הקדוש ברוך הוא's תפילין. The head-תפילין has four separate compartments, but in the arm-תפילין all the verses are written together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them are written together in His arm-תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the earlier discussion about how the praises of ישראל are arranged in הקדוש ברוך הוא's תפילין. This line just finishes that topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא spread the verses across the four compartments of the head-תפילין. Here it adds that the arm-תפילין has only one compartment, so all the verses sit together there. This mirrors how our own תפילין של יד are written on one parchment.

keyTerms.meaning: all of them (here, all the verses)
His arm, meaning His arm-תפילין (תְּפִלִּין שֶׁל יָד)

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the earlier topic of תפילין, not to the בית הכנסת teaching that comes right after it. The new topic starts with the next step.

phrases.english: And all of them are written in His arm-tefillin.
phrases.notes: The arm-תפילין has one compartment, so all the verses are on a single parchment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ כְּתִיבִי בְּאֶדְרָעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer earlier about the arrangement of verses in הקדוש ברוך הוא's תפילין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the head-תפילין the verses are split into four compartments. In the arm-תפילין they are all written together.

steps.title: הקדוש ברוך הוא asks about a regular who misses בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that when someone who regularly comes to בית הכנסת misses one day, הקדוש ברוך הוא asks about him. He brings a פסוק from ישעיהו as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר רב אדא said in the name of רבי יצחק: anyone who usually comes to בית הכנסת and one day does not come, הקדוש ברוך הוא asks about him. As the פסוק says: 'Who among you fears ה', listens to the voice of His servant, who walked in darkness and has no light?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי יצחק says that הקדוש ברוך הוא notices and asks when a regular misses בית הכנסת, and he proves it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק opens with a question, 'מי בכם', which shows הקדוש ברוך הוא asking about someone. 'Listens to the voice of His servant' refers to the חזן leading the תפילה. 'Walked in darkness' describes the person who went out early instead of coming to daven.

keyTerms.meaning: one who is accustomed, a regular
asks about him, inquires after him
as it is said (introduces a proof פָּסוּק)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being consistent in coming to בית הכנסת matters. Once a person is a regular, his absence is noticed above.

phrases.english: Ravin bar Rav Adda said,
Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Anyone who is accustomed to come to the synagogue
and did not come one day,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, asks about him,
as it is said: "Who among you fears the Lord,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו נ:י. The question form shows God 'asking'.

phrases.english: who listens to the voice of His servant,
phrases.notes: His servant is the חזן leading the prayer.

phrases.english: who walked in darkness
phrases.notes: He went out early, before davening.

phrases.english: and has no light."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִין בַּר רַב אַדָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching in the series of statements about תפילה and בית הכנסת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a regular misses בית הכנסת, הקדוש ברוך הוא asks about him (based on ישעיהו נ:י).

steps.title: Light depends on why he was absent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the end of the פסוק. If he missed בית הכנסת for a דבר מצוה, he has light. If he missed it for a דבר הרשות, he has no light.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he went for a מצוה, he has light. If he went for a personal, optional matter, he has no light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the words 'and has no light' by saying the outcome depends on the reason he was away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'he has no light,' but that is not true of everyone who is absent. Someone busy with a מצוה is protected by it, even in darkness. Only someone who skipped for a mundane reason is left without light.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the פסוק as condemning everyone who misses בית הכנסת. The 'no light' applies only to someone who left for a דבר הרשות.

phrases.english: If he went for a matter of a מצוה,
there is light for him,
but if he went for an optional matter,
there is no light for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם לִדְבַר מִצְוָה הָלַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the last words of the פסוק quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Absence for a מצוה brings light. Absence for a mundane matter brings no light.

steps.title: Why is he judged so strictly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the פסוק, 'יבטח בשם ה'', and asks why the person is treated so strictly.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let him trust in the name of ה'.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks for the reason behind this strict treatment, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving for a mundane purpose is not an obvious sin, so why does he get 'no light'? The גמרא points to the continuation of the פסוק as the key to the answer.

phrases.english: "Let him trust in the name of the Lord."
phrases.notes: The continuation of ישעיהו נ:י.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the 'no light' outcome given in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is someone who skipped בית הכנסת for a mundane matter left without light?

steps.title: He should have trusted in God
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he should have trusted in ה' that he would lose nothing by davening first, and he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he should have trusted in the name of ה', and he did not trust.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The problem is that he did not trust ה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He skipped davening because he feared losing out in his business. Had he trusted in ה', he would have davened first and taken care of his affairs afterward. The real failure is a lack of בטחון.
steps.whatToRemember: A regular who misses בית הכנסת is asked about by הקדוש ברוך הוא. If he left for a מצוה, he has light. If he left for a personal matter, he has no light, because he should have had בטחון in ה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that putting personal business ahead of davening reflects a lack of trust in ה'.

phrases.aramaic: — מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לִבְטוֹחַ בְּשֵׁם ה׳,
phrases.english: Because he should have trusted in the name of the Lord,
and he did not trust.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לִבְטוֹחַ בְּשֵׁם ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is judged strictly because he failed to trust in ה' and skipped davening for mundane concerns.

steps.title: הקדוש ברוך הוא becomes angry when there are not ten in the בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that when הקדוש ברוך הוא comes into a בית הכנסת and does not find ten men, He becomes angry right away. He proves it from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: When הקדוש ברוך הוא comes into a בית הכנסת and does not find ten people there, He immediately becomes angry, as it says: 'Why did I come and there is no man? I called and no one answers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן on the same theme of being in בית הכנסת. He says that God is angry when He arrives and there is no מנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי יצחק spoke about one person who misses בית הכנסת. Now רבי יוחנן speaks about the whole community failing to gather ten. The פסוק says 'there is no man' and 'no one answers,' which fits a בית הכנסת where there aren't enough people to answer קדיש and קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten men — a מנין, the minimum needed for public prayer
'Why did I come and there is no man?' (ישעיהו נ:ב)
'And no one answers' — no one to respond to the prayers

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for how serious it is to make sure there is a מנין in בית הכנסת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת,
phrases.english: At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, comes into a synagogue,
and does not find ten people there —
phrases.notes: Ten = a מנין.

phrases.english: He immediately becomes angry,
as it says: 'Why did I come and there is no man?
phrases.notes: ישעיהו נ:ב

phrases.english: I called and there is no one answering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching: after the single person who misses בית הכנסת, now the case of a בית הכנסת without a מנין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When הקדוש ברוך הוא comes to a בית הכנסת and there is no מנין, He is immediately angry.

steps.title: Whoever sets a fixed place for תפילה is helped by the God of אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו in the name of רב הונא teaches that a person who sets a fixed place for his תפילה has the God of אברהם helping him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: Whoever sets a fixed place for his prayer, the God of אברהם is his help.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about davening in the same place every time. Such a person gets special help from the God of אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward is described as 'the God of אברהם' specifically, because (as the גמרא will show) אברהם himself had a fixed place for prayer. So the person is following אברהם's practice, and is helped by אברהם's God.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets (fixes) a place — davens in the same spot regularly

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of having a מקום קבוע — a set place to daven.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said, Rav Huna said:
Anyone who sets a fixed place for his prayer —
the God of Abraham is his help.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל הַקּוֹבֵעַ מָקוֹם לִתְפִלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new teaching about תפילה: not just being in בית הכנסת, but having a set place there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever sets a fixed place for his תפילה is helped by the God of אברהם.

steps.title: He is eulogized as a disciple of אברהם
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the same teaching: when this person dies, people mourn him by calling him humble and pious, one of the students of אברהם אבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he dies, they say about him: 'Where is the humble one? Where is the pious one? He was one of the students of אברהם אבינו!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רב הונא's teaching. It adds the honor this person gets after he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having a fixed place for תפילה marks him as a student of אברהם. The eulogy calls him 'humble' and 'pious,' showing that this small habit reflects a whole character built on אברהם's model.

keyTerms.meaning: Where is...? — a cry of mourning, 'we have lost...'
One of the students of אברהם אבינו

steps.confusionAlert: 'אי עניו' does not mean 'woe' — it means 'Where is the humble one?' It is how people cry out in a eulogy over someone they lost.

phrases.english: And when he dies, they say about him:
'Where is the humble one? Where is the pious one?
One of the disciples of Abraham our father!'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁמֵּת, אוֹמְרִים לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רב הונא's same statement — adds the honor after death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sets a fixed place for תפילה is eulogized as humble, pious, and a student of אברהם אבינו.

steps.title: How do we know אברהם had a fixed place for תפילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that אברהם אבינו had a fixed place for his תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אברהם אבינו — how do we know that he set a fixed place?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask a question about רב הונא's teaching. It sets up the next step, where it will bring a פסוק as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's whole teaching depends on the idea that a fixed place is 'אברהם's way.' So the גמרא wants a source showing that אברהם really did this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? — the גמרא asking for a source
That he set a fixed place

phrases.english: And Abraham our father — from where do we know
that he set a fixed place?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מְנָא לַן דִּקְבַע מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the assumption in steps 7–8 that אברהם had a fixed place.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that אברהם אבינו had a fixed place for his תפילה.

steps.title: אברהם returned to the place where he had stood in תפילה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the תורה says אברהם got up early to 'the place where he had stood.' Since 'standing' means תפילה (as with פינחס), this shows he went back to his set place of prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And אברהם got up early in the morning to the place where he had stood.' And 'standing' always means prayer, as it says: 'And פינחס stood and prayed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a פסוק about אברהם. Then it uses a second פסוק to show that the word 'stood' there means 'prayed.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows אברהם returned to the same place — a fixed place. But it only says he 'stood' there, so the גמרא proves from פינחס's פסוק that 'standing' means תפילה. Together: אברהם went back to the same spot where he had prayed (for סדום).
steps.whatToRemember: Setting a מקום קבוע for תפילה follows אברהם אבינו, who returned to 'the place where he stood' — and 'standing' means תפילה.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof needs two פסוקים. The first only shows אברהם returned to the same place; the second (פינחס) is needed to show that 'stood' means he prayed there.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And Abraham rose early in the morning
phrases.notes: בראשית יט:כז

phrases.english: to the place where he had stood,'
phrases.notes: Where he had prayed for סדום.

phrases.english: and 'standing' means nothing other than prayer,
as it says: 'And Pinchas stood and prayed.'
phrases.notes: תהלים קו:ל

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַד שָׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אברהם returned to 'the place where he stood,' and 'standing' means תפילה (from פינחס), so he had a fixed place of prayer.

steps.title: Do not take large steps when leaving the בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו in the name of רב הונא teaches that a person leaving the בית הכנסת should not take big, hurried steps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: A person who is leaving the בית הכנסת should not take big steps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי חלבו in the name of רב הונא, this time about how to walk out of the בית הכנסת. Taking big steps on the way out looks like you are in a rush to get away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the same series of teachings by רבי חלבו and רב הונא about respect for the בית הכנסת and for תפילה. Rushing out makes it look like davening was a burden you wanted to escape. So the rule says to walk out calmly.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna:
phrases.notes: The same pair of names as the teachings just before this.

phrases.english: One who leaves the synagogue
should not take a large stride.
phrases.notes: Rushing out looks like he wants to get away from the בית הכנסת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new teaching in the same series by רבי חלבו and רב הונא about the בית הכנסת and תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person leaving the בית הכנסת should not take large steps.

steps.title: אביי: the rule is only for leaving, but one should run in
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the rule against big steps applies only to leaving. When entering the בית הכנסת, it is a מצוה to run, based on a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We only said this about going out. But about going in, it is a מצוה to run, as the פסוק says: 'Let us chase after knowing ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets the limits of רב הונא's rule. It applies only to walking out. Walking in is the opposite: you should hurry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule might sound like you should never move quickly near a בית הכנסת. אביי shows that the issue is the message your walking sends. Rushing out looks like escaping, but rushing in shows eagerness, and the פסוק 'נרדפה לדעת את ה׳' praises chasing after closeness to ה׳.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule is simply 'never walk fast in a בית הכנסת.' The direction matters: going out you walk slowly, going in you hurry.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We only said this
phrases.notes: A standard phrase that limits an earlier rule.

phrases.english: about going out.
But for going in, it is a מצוה to run,
as it is said: 'Let us eagerly strive to know ה׳.' (Hoshea 6:3)
phrases.notes: Chasing after ה׳ shows eagerness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא לְמִיפַּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי limits רב הונא's rule to leaving and adds the opposite rule for entering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule against large steps applies only to leaving. When entering, it is a מצוה to run.

steps.title: רבי זירא first thought running on שבת was wrong
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells that at first, when he saw רבנן running to the שיעור on שבת, he thought they were breaking the honor of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: At first, when I used to see the רבנן running to the lecture on שבת, I said: 'The רבנן are desecrating שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא starts a personal story by describing what he used to think. This sets up the next step, where he explains what changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Running on שבת is normally not allowed, because it does not fit the calm and holy feel of the day. So רבי זירא saw a real problem when he watched the רבנן running. This is the question his story will now answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A public תורה lecture (שיעור), often given on שבת

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: At first,
when I would see the Rabbis
running to the lecture on Shabbos,
I said: 'The Rabbis are desecrating Shabbos.'
phrases.notes: Running on שבת goes against the calm, holy feel of the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מֵרֵישׁ כִּי הֲוָה חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of running for a מצוה and raises a possible problem: what about running on שבת?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא's first view was that running on שבת, even to a שיעור, looked like breaking the honor of שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: run to learn הלכה even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא heard the teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי that one should always run to learn הלכה, even on שבת, based on a פסוק. From then on, he ran too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once I heard what רבי תנחום said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, 'A person should always run to a matter of הלכה, even on שבת, as it says: They will follow ה׳, who roars like a lion,' I also run.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains what changed his mind: a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי that running to Torah learning is proper even on שבת. So he started running as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry from the last step was that running on שבת is wrong. רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that running to learn הלכה is different, because the פסוק 'אחרי ה׳ ילכו כאריה ישאג' describes people rushing to follow ה׳. Running for תורה shows eagerness, so it does not break the honor of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: To a matter of תורה law / learning
He will roar like a lion

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the basis for the idea that running to a שיעור or to תפילה is allowed and even praised on שבת, while running for ordinary reasons is not.

phrases.english: Once I heard this teaching

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: of Rabbi Tanchum, who said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
A person should always run to a matter of halacha,
and even on Shabbos,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַחֲרֵי ה׳ יֵלְכוּ כְּאַרְיֵה יִשְׁאָג״ וְגוֹ׳,
phrases.english: as it is said: 'They shall walk after ה׳, who will roar like a lion,' etc. (Hoshea 11:10)
phrases.notes: People rush after ה׳, like people running when a lion roars.

phrases.english: I too run.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לְהָא דְּרַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's earlier worry that running on שבת was wrong.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a source showing that running for Torah learning is an exception to the usual rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Running on שבת is always disrespectful to the day, even when running to a שיעור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Running to learn הלכה is proper even on שבת, so רבי זירא runs too.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the reward for a שיעור is for the running
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא teaches that the main reward for going to a פרקא comes from running to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The reward for the lecture is the running.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives a short saying about where the reward for attending a שיעור comes from. The main reward is for the eagerness of rushing there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many people at a public שיעור did not fully understand what was taught. Even so, they get great reward for their eagerness, which they showed by running to come and hear תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
The reward for the lecture is the running.
phrases.notes: Even someone who did not understand much still gets reward for his eagerness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אַגְרָא דְפִרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the running to the פרקא described in the story before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for going to a פרקא comes from the eagerness of running to it.

steps.title: אביי: the reward for a כלה is for the crowding
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a similar saying: the main reward for going to a כלה gathering comes from putting up with the crowding.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The reward for the כלה is the crowding.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a saying that matches רבי זירא's. At the big כלה learning gatherings, the reward comes from putting up with the crowded conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כלה gatherings were very crowded, which made it hard to learn much. The reward comes from the effort and discomfort a person accepts in order to hear תורה. Together with the last step, this teaches that ה׳ rewards the effort, not only what you understood.

keyTerms.meaning: Large public learning gathering, held in אדר and אלול

steps.whatToRemember: Leave the בית הכנסת calmly, but hurry to go in. Running to learn תורה is praised even on שבת. Much of the reward for learning תורה comes from the effort, like rushing and putting up with crowds, even when you do not understand everything.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The reward for the kallah is the crowding.
phrases.notes: The reward comes from the effort of putting up with the crowd.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אַגְרָא דְכַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A matching saying to רבי זירא's teaching about the reward for a פרקא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for going to a כלה comes from putting up with the crowding.

steps.title: The reward of learning is understanding the reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds to the list: the main reward for learning שמעתא comes from the סברא, the reasoning behind it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The main reward for learning a teaching is for the reasoning, meaning understanding why it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another saying in the same pattern as רבי זירא and אביי. He says that when you learn, the main reward is for working to understand the reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply knowing the final הלכה is not where most of the reward lies. The reward comes from the mental effort of understanding the סברא, meaning the logic that leads to the conclusion. This fits the theme of these sayings: the reward is in the hard, inner part of the action.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or halachic tradition that one learns

steps.whyThisMatters: This saying is often quoted to show that learning means understanding, not just memorizing conclusions.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The reward of a teaching is the reasoning.
phrases.notes: The main reward for learning comes from the effort of understanding the logic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַגְרָא דִשְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another 'אַגְרָא' saying in the same pattern as רבי זירא and אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for learning תורה is for understanding the reasoning (סברא).

steps.title: The reward of visiting mourners is silence
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the main reward for going to a בית האבל comes from sitting quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The main reward for going to a house of mourning is for the silence.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא continues the list. He says that when you visit a mourner, the main reward is for being quiet with him, not for talking a lot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being there in silence shows real care for the mourner. Too many words can hurt more than they help. Again the reward lies in the harder inner part of the act, which here is self-control and sensitivity.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The reward of a house of mourning is silence.
phrases.notes: Sitting quietly with the mourner is the main source of reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אַגְרָא דְבֵי טַמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next saying in the same 'אַגְרָא' list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for comforting mourners is for the silence there.

steps.title: The reward of a fast is the charity given
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the main reward of a תענית comes from the צדקה given to the poor on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: The main reward for fasting is for the charity given.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא adds his saying to the list. He says the main reward of a fast day comes from the צדקה people give, not only from going hungry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not eating alone is not the main point of a תענית. The fast should lead a person to help others, for example by giving the poor food for the night. This matches the message of ישעיה פרק נח, which says that the fast ה׳ wants includes sharing bread with the hungry.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
The reward of a fast is charity.
phrases.notes: The צדקה given to the poor on the fast day is the main source of reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: אַגְרָא דְתַעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next saying in the same 'אַגְרָא' list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for fasting is for the צדקה given on the fast day.

steps.title: The reward of a eulogy is making people cry out
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the main reward of a הספד comes from raising the voice and moving the listeners to cry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The main reward for a eulogy is for raising the voice, meaning stirring people so they cry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds another saying to this list. He says the main reward of a הספד is for speaking in a way that moves people to raise their voices and cry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הספד is not just a speech of facts about the person who died. Its goal is to make people truly feel the loss. The reward comes from stirring real grief.

keyTerms.meaning: Raising, lifting up (the voice), meaning stirring people to cry out

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
The reward of a eulogy is raising the voice.
phrases.notes: Moving the listeners to cry aloud over the person who died is the main source of reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אַגְרָא דְהֶסְפֵּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next saying in the same 'אַגְרָא' list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for a הספד is for raising voices and stirring people to cry.

steps.title: The main reward for joining a wedding is the words
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds the last item to the 'main reward' list: at a wedding, the main reward comes from the words of blessing and joy said to the חתן and כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The main reward for going to a wedding is for the words.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds one more line to the chain of 'the main reward of X is Y' sayings from the previous steps. For a wedding, the main reward comes from the words said to make the couple happy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier sayings, this points to the hidden core of a מצוה. Showing up and eating at a wedding is not the main point. The main reward comes from the words of praise and blessing that bring joy to the חתן and כלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Words (here: words of blessing and praise for the couple)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole list of seven sayings (steps 15–21) teaches one idea: every מצוה has a 'main part' where most of the reward lies. In a פרקא it is running, in a כלה it is putting up with crowding, in learning it is the סברא, with mourners it is silence, in a fast it is צדקה, in a הספד it is stirring real grief, and at a wedding it is the words of joy. That part is often the effort or the inner content, not just showing up.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The reward for a wedding is for the words.
phrases.notes: The words of blessing and praise said to bring joy to the bride and groom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַגְרָא דְבֵי הִלּוּלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item in the chain of 'main reward' sayings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The main reward for joining a wedding comes from the words that bring the couple joy.

steps.title: One who prays behind the בית הכנסת is called a רשע
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that someone who prays behind a בית הכנסת is called a רשע. He supports this with the פסוק 'סביב רשעים יתהלכון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Anyone who prays behind the בית הכנסת is called a 'רשע,' as it says: 'The wicked walk all around' (תהלים 12:9).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of honoring a בית הכנסת. רב הונא says that praying behind a בית הכנסת earns a person the label רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the whole congregation faces one way, this person stands behind the building and faces the other way. That looks like he is turning his back on the בית הכנסת and the people praying inside. The פסוק says the wicked 'walk around,' meaning they stay on the outside edge instead of facing in the right direction.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Anyone who prays behind the synagogue
phrases.notes: He faces the opposite way from the congregation, as if turning his back on them.

phrases.english: is called 'wicked,'
as it is said: 'The wicked walk all around.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 12:9. Read as: the wicked go around to the back of the בית הכנסת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'main reward' list and returns to the earlier topic of respect for the בית הכנסת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying behind the בית הכנסת (facing away from it) makes one a רשע, based on 'סביב רשעים יתהלכון'.

steps.title: אביי limits the rule to someone who does not face the בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רב הונא's rule only applies when the person does not turn his face toward the בית הכנסת. If he does face it, there is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We only said this when he does not turn his face toward the בית הכנסת. But if he turns his face toward the בית הכנסת, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows רב הונא's rule. The problem is not standing behind the building. The problem is facing away from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, you might think any spot behind the בית הכנסת is forbidden. אביי teaches that the real issue is the direction you face. If you stand behind the building but turn toward it, you are facing the same way as the congregation, so there is no disrespect.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when… (a formula that limits a rule)
We have no problem with it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי disagrees with רב הונא. He accepts the rule and only defines its limits: what matters is which way you face, not where you stand.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We only said this
where he does not turn his face toward the synagogue,
but if he turns his face toward the synagogue —
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב הונא's rule to one specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban applies only when one faces away from the בית הכנסת. Facing toward it is allowed.

steps.title: אליהו kills a man who prayed facing away from the בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: A story: a man prayed behind a בית הכנסת without facing it. אליהו הנביא, looking like an Arab, rebuked him and killed him with a sword. This shows how serious the sin is.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who was praying behind the בית הכנסת and did not turn his face toward the בית הכנסת. אליהו passed by and saw him. He appeared to him as an Arab. He said to him: 'Is this how you stand before your Master?!' He drew a sword and killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that matches the forbidden case exactly: behind the בית הכנסת and not facing it. It shows how seriously Heaven treats this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man fits the exact case אביי described, so the story confirms רב הונא's rule as אביי limited it. אליהו's words, 'Is this how you stand before your Master?!', explain the sin: facing away during תפילה is disrespect to ה׳. The harsh ending shows the label רשע is no exaggeration.
steps.whatToRemember: Final rule of this section: praying behind a בית הכנסת while facing away from it is very serious (רשע). Facing toward the בית הכנסת removes the problem.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is often quoted to show that the direction we face in תפילה is a matter of real respect before ה׳, not just a technical detail.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who was praying
behind the synagogue,
and he did not turn his face toward the synagogue.
phrases.notes: Exactly the forbidden case from אביי.

phrases.english: Elijah passed by.
He saw him; he appeared to him as an Arab,
He said to him:
Is this how you stand before your Master?!
He drew a sword and killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא גַבְרָא דְּקָא מְצַלֵּי אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּי כְּנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that illustrates and backs up the rule of רב הונא, as limited by אביי.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule (as limited by אביי) that praying behind the בית הכנסת while facing away is a grave sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of אליהו killing a man who prayed facing away from the בית הכנסת.

steps.title: What does 'כרם זלות לבני אדם' mean?
steps.stepSummary: One of the Rabbis asks רב ביבי בר אביי what the end of רב הונא's פסוק means. Some say the question was asked by רב ביבי to רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Rabbis said to רב ביבי בר אביי, and some say רב ביבי said to רב נחמן בר יצחק: What is the meaning of 'כְּרֻם זֻלּוּת לִבְנֵי אָדָם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the second half of the פסוק that רב הונא quoted, and asks what it means. This question sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא only used the first half of the פסוק, 'סביב רשעים יתהלכון'. The words 'כרם זלות לבני אדם' are hard to understand, so someone asks for their meaning. The גמרא also records two versions of who asked whom.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: a second version of who said it
A hard word in the פסוק. It can mean 'when it is raised up,' or it can be the name of a bird

phrases.english: One of the Rabbis said
to Rav Beivai bar Abaye,
and some say Rav Beivai said it
phrases.notes: A second version of who asked the question.

phrases.english: to Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak:
What is the meaning of 'When vileness is exalted among the sons of men'?
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the פסוק that רב הונא quoted in Step 22.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כְּרֻם זֻלּוּת לִבְנֵי אָדָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the פסוק from Step 22 and asks about its second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'כרם זלות לבני אדם'.

steps.title: Lofty matters that people treat lightly
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק is talking about things that stand at the top of the world, but people treat them lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: These are things that stand at the very top of the world, yet people treat them with disrespect.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. 'כרם' means 'high up,' and 'זלות' means people treat it as cheap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כרם is read as 'רום', meaning height. So the פסוק describes very important things, such as תפלה, that people look down on. This fits the topic of רב הונא's statement about praying behind a בית הכנסת.

keyTerms.meaning: At the height of the world, meaning things of the greatest importance

phrases.english: He said to him: These are matters
that stand at the height of the world,
phrases.notes: This reads כרם as 'רום', meaning height. Examples are תפלה and מצוות.

phrases.english: and people treat them with contempt.
phrases.notes: This explains 'זלות לבני אדם'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁעוֹמְדִים בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק refers to lofty matters, like תפלה, that people treat lightly.

steps.title: Depending on others makes a person's face change
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר explain the פסוק in a different way. When a person needs help from other people, his face changes color like a כרום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר both said: Once a person needs other people, his face changes like a כרום, as it says, 'כְּרֻם זֻלּוּת לִבְנֵי אָדָם'.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give a second, different explanation of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'כרם' does not mean height. It is the name of something that changes its look. 'זלות לבני אדם' describes the shame of depending on other people. That shame makes a person's face change color.

keyTerms.meaning: Needs other people, depends on them

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a continuation of the first answer. It is a completely different reading of the word כרם. Before, it meant 'height.' Here, it is a creature that changes color.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar
who both said:
Once a person needs other people,
his face changes like a kerum,
as it is stated: 'Like a kerum is the lowering of people.'
phrases.notes: Here the פסוק is read as: 'Like a כרום, when a person is lowered before others.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the same פסוק that Step 26 explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Depending on other people causes shame that changes a person's face, like a כרום.

steps.title: What is a כרום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the כרום is that רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a 'כרום'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word כרום means in רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר's explanation. This sets up רב דימי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their explanation depends on comparing a face to a כרום, but they did not say what a כרום is. Without that, we cannot understand the comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: The thing a changing face is compared to (explained in the next step)

phrases.english: What is a 'kerum'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כְּרוּם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word used in Step 27.

steps.title: רב דימי: the כרום is a color-changing bird
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains that the כרום is a bird in the coastal cities that changes into many colors when the sun shines on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: There is a bird in the cities by the sea, and its name is כרום. When the sun rises, it changes into many colors.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question by identifying the כרום as a bird that changes colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the comparison makes sense. Just as this bird turns many colors in the sunlight, a person who must ask others for help turns red and pale from embarrassment.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of 'כרם זלות לבני אדם'. (1) Lofty things, like תפלה, that people treat lightly. (2) The shame of depending on others, which makes a person's face change colors like the כרום bird.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
There is a certain bird in the cities by the sea,
and its name is 'kerum,'
and once the sun shines,
it changes into several colors.
phrases.notes: This is like a person's face changing from embarrassment.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כרום is a bird in the coastal cities that changes into many colors when the sun rises.

steps.title: Needing others is like being punished with fire and water
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי and רבי אסי give another description of how painful it is to depend on other people. They say it is like being punished with both fire and water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי both say: it is as if he was judged with two punishments, fire and water. As the פסוק says: 'You let men ride over our heads; we went through fire and water.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still talking about a person who needs help from others. רבי אמי and רבי אסי add one more way to describe how painful that is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר said the person's face changes colors like the כרום bird. רבי אמי and רבי אסי go further: it feels like two harsh punishments at once. They learn this from a פסוק where 'men riding over our heads' (being under other people's control) is linked to going 'through fire and water.'

keyTerms.meaning: You let men ride over our heads, meaning being under other people's control

steps.whatToRemember: Needing other people is described in strong terms. The face changes colors like the כרום, and it feels like being punished by fire and water together.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, who both say:
phrases.notes: Like רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר before them, these two אמוראים speak together about the pain of depending on others.

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִלּוּ נִדּוֹן בִּשְׁנֵי דִינִים, אֵשׁ וּמַיִם,
phrases.english: It is as if he was judged with two punishments, fire and water,
as it says: 'You let men ride over our heads,'
phrases.notes: תהלים ס״ו:י״ב

phrases.english: 'we went through fire and water.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger description of depending on others, next to the כרום explanation of רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Depending on other people is like being punished with both fire and water.

steps.title: Be extra careful with the afternoon prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו quotes רב הונא: a person must always be careful with תפלת המנחה, because אליהו was answered at the time of מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: a person should always be careful with תפלת המנחה, because אליהו was answered only during תפלת המנחה. As it says: 'And it was at the time of the מנחה offering, and אליהו the prophet came close and said... Answer me, ה׳, answer me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement from the same chain, רבי חלבו in the name of רב הונא. It teaches that תפלת המנחה needs special care.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from אליהו on הר הכרמל. His prayer was answered with fire from heaven 'at the time of the מנחה offering.' Since such a great answer came at מנחה time, that prayer has special power, so a person should take it seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time the afternoon offering is brought up

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for treating מנחה with special seriousness. It is easy to neglect מנחה because it falls in the middle of a busy day.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא אָדָם זָהִיר בִּתְפִלַּת הַמִּנְחָה,
phrases.english: A person should always be careful with the afternoon prayer,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ לֹא נַעֲנָה אֶלָּא בִּתְפִלַּת הַמִּנְחָה,
phrases.english: because Eliyahu was answered only in the afternoon prayer,
as it says: 'And it was at the time of the afternoon offering,'
phrases.notes: מלכים א י״ח:ל״ו-ל״ז

phrases.english: 'and Eliyahu the prophet came close and said, etc.'
'Answer me, ה׳, answer me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about the importance of a specific prayer. It is linked to the earlier material only by the same chain of transmission, רבי חלבו and רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must always be careful with תפלת המנחה, since אליהו was answered at מנחה time.

steps.title: Why אליהו said 'answer me' twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the double 'ענני'. The first was a request for fire to come down. The second was a request that the people would not call it sorcery.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Answer me': that fire should come down from heaven. And 'answer me' again: that they should not say it is an act of sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: Along the way, the גמרא explains why the פסוק says 'ענני' two times. Each one was a separate request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first request was for the miracle itself, fire from heaven. The second was that the people would understand the miracle correctly, as coming from ה׳ and not from כשפים. A miracle only helps if people accept where it came from.

keyTerms.meaning: An act of sorcery or magic

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second 'ענני' is just repeating the first for emphasis. The גמרא teaches that it was a completely different request: for the people's belief, not for the fire.

phrases.english: 'Answer me': that fire should come down from heaven,

phrases.aramaic: וַ״עֲנֵנִי״ — שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ מַעֲשֵׂה כְשָׁפִים הֵם.
phrases.english: and 'answer me': that they should not say it is an act of sorcery.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עֲנֵנִי״ — שֶׁתֵּרֵד אֵשׁ מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side explanation of the פסוק quoted in Step 31. It explains why the word 'ענני' appears twice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two 'ענני's were two separate requests: one for the fire and one so the people would not say it was כשפים.

steps.title: The evening prayer also needs care
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that a person must also be careful with תפלת ערבית. He brings a פסוק that compares prayer to the evening offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: also with תפלת ערבית. As it says: 'Let my prayer be set up as incense before You, the lifting of my hands as the evening offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds to רב הונא's teaching. Not only מנחה, but ערבית also needs special care.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' (also) shows that רבי יוחנן agrees about מנחה and adds ערבית to the list. His proof is a פסוק in תהלים that links prayer to the 'מנחת ערב', the evening offering.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף בִּתְפִלַּת עַרְבִית,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: also with the evening prayer,
as it says: 'Let my prayer be set up as incense before You,'
phrases.notes: תהלים קמ״א:ב׳

phrases.english: 'the lifting of my hands as the evening offering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף בִּתְפִלַּת עַרְבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רב הונא's rule about מנחה so that it also includes ערבית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must also be careful with תפלת ערבית.

steps.title: The morning prayer also needs care
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that a person must also be careful with תפלת שחרית. He brings a פסוק about praying in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: also with תפלת שחרית. As it says: 'ה׳, in the morning You will hear my voice; in the morning I will set out my prayer to You and wait.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds one more prayer, שחרית. Now all three daily prayers have been named as needing special care.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the word 'אף' adds to the list without arguing against the earlier opinions. His proof is a פסוק that says twice that prayer is set out 'בקר', in the morning.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא says to be careful with מנחה because of אליהו. רבי יוחנן adds ערבית. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds שחרית. Each one brings a פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַף תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: also the morning prayer,
as it says: 'ה׳, in the morning You will hear my voice;'
phrases.notes: תהלים ה׳:ד׳

phrases.english: 'in the morning I will set out my prayer to You and wait.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: אַף תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the list one more time, adding שחרית after רבי יוחנן added ערבית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must also be careful with תפלת שחרית.

steps.title: Enjoying a wedding meal without gladdening the groom
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו quotes רב הונא: anyone who benefits from a חתן's meal and does not make him happy 'violates the five voices' of the פסוק in ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: Anyone who enjoys the meal of a groom and does not make him happy goes against the 'five voices', as the פסוק says: 'The voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the groom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who say: Give thanks to the Lord of hosts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same chain, רבי חלבו quoting רב הונא. It says that eating at a wedding without making the חתן happy is a serious failing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a guest at a wedding is not just about eating. You take on a responsibility to bring joy to the חתן. The פסוק lists five 'voices' of wedding joy, and a guest who ignores this goes against all five of them.

keyTerms.meaning: the wedding feast of a groom

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna:
Anyone who benefits from the feast of a groom
and does not make him happy
violates the five voices,
as it says: 'The voice of joy and the voice of gladness,
the voice of the groom and the voice of the bride,
phrases.notes: ירמיה ל״ג:י״א

phrases.aramaic: קוֹל אוֹמְרִים הוֹדוּ אֶת ה׳ צְבָאוֹת״.
phrases.english: the voice of those who say: Give thanks to the Lord of hosts.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the same chain of רבי חלבו quoting רב הונא (compare step 31), now on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A guest who benefits from a wedding meal must gladden the חתן; failing to do so violates the five voices of ירמיה ל״ג:י״א.

steps.title: What is the reward for gladdening the groom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the flip side: if a guest does make the חתן happy, what reward does he get?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he does make him happy, what is his reward?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next teaching. Now that it knows the punishment, it asks about the reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 described only the negative side. This question opens the positive side and prepares for רבי יהושע בן לוי's answer.

phrases.english: And if he makes him happy, what is his reward?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם מְשַׂמְּחוֹ מַה שְּׂכָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the positive counterpart of the punishment described in step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reward for one who gladdens the חתן.

steps.title: He merits the תורה, which was given with five voices
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers that he merits the תורה, which was given with five voices. The voices are counted from פסוקים in שמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: He merits the תורה, which was given with five voices, as it says: 'And on the third day, in the morning, there were voices and lightning and a heavy cloud on the mountain, and the voice of a שופר.' And: 'The voice of the שופר grew stronger, and God answered him with a voice.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers the question. Making the חתן happy earns a person the תורה, which also came with five voices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward matches the deed: five voices of joy for the חתן earn the five voices of מתן תורה. The count works like this: 'קֹלֹת' is plural, so it counts as two. Add 'קול שופר' (three), 'קול השופר' (four), and 'בקול' (five).

keyTerms.meaning: voices/sounds (plural, so it counts as two)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't count 'קֹלֹת' as one voice. A plural means at least two, and that is how we reach five.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
He merits the Torah, which was given with five voices,
as it says: 'And it was on the third day, when it was morning,
phrases.notes: שמות י״ט:ט״ז

phrases.english: there were voices and lightning
phrases.notes: Plural, so this counts as 2 voices

phrases.english: and a heavy cloud upon the mountain
and the voice of a shofar, etc.'
phrases.notes: Voice 3

phrases.english: 'And the voice of the shofar, etc.
phrases.notes: שמות י״ט:י״ט; voice 4

phrases.english: and God answered him with a voice.'
phrases.notes: Voice 5

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: זוֹכֶה לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּתְּנָה בַּחֲמִשָּׁה קוֹלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He merits the תורה, given with five voices, which are counted from שמות י״ט:ט״ז and י״ט:י״ט.

steps.title: Challenge: another verse mentions more voices at סיני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the count of five is correct, since another פסוק says 'all the people saw the voices', which adds more voices.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But it is written: 'And all the people saw the voices'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי's count of exactly five voices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק in שמות כ׳ also describes 'voices' at הר סיני. Since that is another plural, it seems to add at least two more voices, so the total should be more than five.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כְּתִיב ״וְכׇל הָעָם רוֹאִים אֶת הַקּוֹלוֹת״!
phrases.english: But it is written: 'And all the people saw the voices'!
phrases.notes: שמות כ׳:ט״ו

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִּי? וְהָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the count of five voices from step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תורה was given with exactly five voices.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמות כ׳:ט״ו mentions additional plural 'voices', so the total seems to be more than five.

steps.title: Those voices came before מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the voices in that פסוק happened before מתן תורה, so they are not part of the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those voices were before the giving of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the extra voices do not count, because they came before the actual giving of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only voices that came with מתן תורה itself are counted. The voices mentioned in שמות כ׳ belong to the earlier lead-up, so the total of five stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: Gladdening a חתן (five voices of joy) earns the תורה (five voices at סיני). Failing to do it while enjoying his meal violates those five voices.

phrases.english: Those voices
were before the giving of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתָן קוֹלוֹת, דְּקוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing distinction: the extra voices came before מתן תורה, so they are excluded from the count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every mention of voices at סיני counts toward the total, which would make it more than five.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the voices that came with מתן תורה itself count, so the total is five.

steps.title: Making a groom happy is like bringing a thanksgiving offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו gives a different answer to the question of the reward: it is as if the guest brought a קרבן תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is as if he brought a thanksgiving offering, as the פסוק says: 'Those who bring a thanksgiving offering to the house of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question from Step 36, 'What reward does someone get for making the חתן happy?', and gives a second answer from רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי said the reward is תורה. רבי אבהו reads further in the same פסוק in ירמיה, which talks about the joy of a חתן and כלה. That פסוק goes on to say 'מביאים תודה בית ה׳', so he says making the couple happy is like bringing a קרבן תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: as if; it is considered as though

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The פסוק 'מביאים תודה' is the same פסוק in ירמיה that lists the five voices (קול חתן וקול כלה). רבי אבהו is simply reading the next words of it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
It is as if he offered a thanksgiving offering,
phrases.notes: This is the reward for making the groom happy.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Those who bring a thanksgiving offering to the house of ה׳.'
phrases.notes: ירמיה 33:11, the same פסוק as the five voices.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר: כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרִיב תּוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about counting the voices (Steps 38-39), the גמרא returns to the question of Step 36 and offers another answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reward is as if he brought a קרבן תודה, learned from 'מביאים תודה בית ה׳' in the same פסוק.

steps.title: Making a groom happy is like rebuilding a ruin of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a third answer: it is as if the guest rebuilt one of the ruins of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is as if he built one of the ruins of ירושלים, as the פסוק says: 'For I will bring back the captivity of the land as at first, says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more answer to the same question about the reward for making a חתן happy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the very end of the same פסוק in ירמיה, which talks about restoring the land to how it was before. So bringing joy to a חתן and כלה is like helping rebuild ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: the captives; the exiled state (which ה׳ will bring back)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers for the reward of making a חתן happy, and all of them come from the same פסוק in ירמיה: תורה (רבי יהושע בן לוי), a קרבן תודה (רבי אבהו), and rebuilding ירושלים (רב נחמן בר יצחק).

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is as if he built one of the ruins of Jerusalem,
as it says: 'For I will bring back the captivity of the land
as it was at first, says ה׳.'
phrases.notes: The end of the same פסוק in ירמיה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: כְּאִילּוּ בָּנָה אַחַת מֵחוּרְבוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative answer to the same question, taken from the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The reward is as if he rebuilt one of the ruins of ירושלים, learned from 'כי אשיב את שבות הארץ כבראשונה'.

steps.title: A God-fearing person's words are listened to
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו, quoting רב הונא, teaches that anyone who has יראת שמים will have his words heard, based on a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חלבו said in the name of רב הונא: Any person who has fear of Heaven, his words are listened to, as the פסוק says: 'The end of the matter, everything is heard: fear God, and so on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching from the same pair of רבי חלבו and רב הונא. It is about the power of a person who fears ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in קהלת says 'everything is heard' right next to 'fear God'. רב הונא reads this as a link: the person who fears God is the one whose words get heard. The 'וגו׳' stands for the rest of the פסוק, 'and keep His commandments, for this is all of man', which the גמרא explains next.

keyTerms.meaning: fear of Heaven; awe of ה׳
'and so on', meaning the פסוק continues

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna:
phrases.notes: This is the same pair as in Step 35, with a new teaching.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם —
phrases.english: Any person who has fear of Heaven,
his words are listened to,
as it says: 'The end of the matter, everything is heard:
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:13.

phrases.english: fear God, and so on.'
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק is: 'and keep His commandments, for this is all of man.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same speakers (רבי חלבו quoting רב הונא), added because of the shared names, not because the topic continues.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person with יראת שמים has his words listened to, learned from 'הכל נשמע את האלהים ירא'.

steps.title: What does 'this is all of man' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the end of the פסוק in קהלת means: 'for this is all of man'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'for this is all of man' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the last words of the פסוק just quoted mean. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'כי זה כל האדם' is unclear. How can one God-fearing person be 'all of man'? The גמרא asks for an explanation, and three answers follow.

keyTerms.meaning: all of man; the whole of mankind

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'כי זה כל האדם' were not quoted in Step 42. They are hidden inside the 'וגו׳'. The גמרא is asking about the end of the same פסוק from קהלת.

phrases.english: What does 'for this is all of man' mean?
phrases.notes: 'This' refers to the God-fearing person who keeps the מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כִּי זֶה כׇּל הָאָדָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the end of the פסוק used as the source in Step 42.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase 'כי זה כל האדם' at the end of the פסוק in קהלת.

steps.title: The whole world was created for this person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that הקב״ה said the entire world was created only for the sake of such a God-fearing person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: הקב״ה said, 'The entire world was created only for the sake of this person.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the first answer to the question of what 'this is all of man' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אלעזר's reading, 'all of man' means the whole world exists for this person. The God-fearing person is the purpose of creation.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He (ה׳)

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
The entire world was not created
except for the sake of this person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 43.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'All of man' means the entire world was created only for the God-fearing person.

steps.title: This person is equal to the whole world
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא explains that a God-fearing person is equal in worth to the entire world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא said: This person is equal to the entire world.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to what 'this is all of man' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא בר כהנא does not say the world was made for him. He says the God-fearing person weighs the same as the whole world. 'All of man' means he is worth as much as everyone together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁקוּל זֶה כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: This person is equal to the entire world.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: שָׁקוּל זֶה כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the same phrase than רבי אלעזר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'All of man' means the God-fearing person is equal in worth to the whole world.

steps.title: The whole world was created to be companions for this person
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי (some say בן זומא) explains that the entire world was created to keep the God-fearing person company.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן עזאי says, and some say רבי שמעון בן זומא says: The entire world was created only to be companions for this person.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer to what 'this is all of man' means. The גמרא is unsure which תנא said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view is close to רבי אלעזר's, but it is more specific. The rest of the world exists so the God-fearing person will have people around him to live with and interact with. The 'ואמרי לה' shows that there was a doubt about who said it.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (it was someone else)
to accompany; to be company for

steps.whatToRemember: The three explanations of 'כי זה כל האדם' are: the world was created for this person (רבי אלעזר); he equals the whole world (רבי אבא בר כהנא); the world was created to keep him company (בן עזאי or בן זומא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma says:
phrases.notes: There is a doubt about which תנא said this.

phrases.english: The entire world was not created
except to be companions for this person.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third explanation of the same phrase, which finishes the list of answers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'All of man' means the whole world was created to be companions for the God-fearing person.

steps.title: Greet first someone who usually greets you
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו, quoting רב הונא, teaches that if you know your friend usually greets you, you should greet him first, as the פסוק says 'Seek peace and pursue it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חלבו said that רב הונא said: Anyone who knows that his friend usually greets him should greet him first, as it says: 'Seek peace and pursue it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same pair, רבי חלבו quoting רב הונא. It is a rule of good behavior: don't wait to be greeted, greet first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from the double language of the פסוק. 'Seek peace' is not enough; you must also 'pursue it,' meaning go after it actively. So it is not enough to answer a greeting. You should be the one who starts it.

keyTerms.meaning: He should greet him first (be first to say שלום)
Seek peace and pursue it (תהלים ל״ד)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that שלום is not passive. A person is expected to go out of his way to create friendly relationships, not just to respond politely.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥelbo said that Rav Huna said:
phrases.notes: Same chain of tradition as the earlier teachings in this section.

phrases.english: Anyone who knows about his fellow
that he is accustomed to greet him,
phrases.notes: Literally 'to give him peace,' meaning to say hello.

phrases.english: should greet him first,
as it is stated: 'Seek peace and pursue it.'
phrases.notes: תהלים ל״ד:ט״ו. 'Pursue' means actively running after peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of יראת שמים to a new teaching from the same רבי חלבו / רב הונא chain about greeting others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If you know someone usually greets you, you should greet him first, based on 'בקש שלום ורדפהו'.

steps.title: Not returning a greeting is called robbery
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the same teaching: if someone greeted a person and he did not answer, he is called a גזלן, based on the פסוק 'the theft of the poor is in your houses.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the other person greeted him and he did not answer back, he is called a robber, as it says: 'You have eaten up the vineyard; the theft of the poor is in your houses.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא's teaching continues with the opposite case: someone greets you and you ignore him. The גמרא says this person is called a גזלן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof uses the words 'theft of the poor.' A poor person has nothing to steal, so what can you steal from him? Only his greeting and his dignity. Ignoring his שלום is like taking something that belongs to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The theft of the poor (ישעיה ג׳)
You have eaten up (destroyed) the vineyard

steps.confusionAlert: This is not literal money robbery. The poor man in the פסוק owns nothing, so the 'theft' must be of something that is not money: his greeting and his honor.
steps.whatToRemember: Two levels: greet first (בקש שלום ורדפהו), and at the very least answer a greeting. Ignoring one makes you a גזלן.

phrases.english: And if he greeted him and he did not return the greeting —
he is called a 'robber,'
as it is stated: 'It is you who have eaten up the vineyard,'
phrases.notes: ישעיה ג׳:י״ד.

phrases.english: the theft of the poor is in your houses.'
phrases.notes: A poor man has nothing to steal except his greeting, so this refers to ignoring his שלום.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם נָתַן לוֹ וְלֹא הֶחֱזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same רב הונא teaching. It moves from the ideal (greet first) to the minimum (at least answer back).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who does not return a greeting is called a גזלן, based on 'גזלת העני בבתיכם'.
